column5: we seek from God a straight way
column6: Ezra proclaims a fast so the traveling community may seek from God a straight way for themselves, their children, and their goods; it closely joins communal petition, dependence, and the requested road.

column5: God's hand helps travelers on the road
column6: Ezra contrasts royal military help with God's favorable hand on those who seek him while facing enemies on the way; it gives nasta'inu a travel-specific account of divine aid.

column5: fasting and entreating God for the journey
column6: The community fasts and entreats God for the safe journey, and God answers; it supplies a concrete liturgical continuation of asking help before setting out.

column5: donkey collapsed under a burden
column6: The law requires helping even an enemy's donkey when it lies under its load; it gives the commentary's exhausted mount an ethical command not to leave it stranded.

column5: fallen donkey on the road; lift it up
column6: The law forbids ignoring a fellow Israelite's fallen donkey on the road and requires raising it with the owner; it directly answers the source's stopped mount with shared assistance.

column5: traveler asks guarding, food, and clothing
column6: Jacob asks that God be with him, guard him on the way, and provide bread and clothing; it gives the vulnerable traveler a prayer for both protection and material support.

column5: guide on a way not traveled before
column6: The ark goes ahead so Israel will know the way to go because it has not passed that way before; it is a precise narrative of a guide for people unable to orient themselves alone.

column5: 'ayn-b-d B007/B011; walk all God's ways
column6: Deuteronomy couples walking in all God's ways with serving God from the whole heart; Hebrew avad is cognate with the source label for na'budu and preserves its worship-and-way sequence.

column5: 'ayn-b-d B007/B011; service and bodily healing
column6: Israel is to serve God, who blesses bread and water and removes sickness; the Hebrew avad cognate places service beside the bodily strengthening the commentary associates with aid.

column5: mercy leads and guides to water
column6: The hungry and thirsty are protected from scorching because the merciful one leads and guides them to springs; it gives the source's needy traveler both relief and a destination.

column5: build up the way; remove obstruction
column6: God commands that a road be built and every obstruction removed from the people's way; it turns the commentary's support and wall imagery into preparation for safe passage.

column5: carry, bear, and save through frailty
column6: God promises to carry and bear people even into old age and gray hair; it supplies a sustained divine counterpart to the source's body that needs to be held up.

column5: assemble the lame and afflicted
column6: God will gather the lame, the outcast, and those afflicted; it makes the physically impaired people in the source an object of restoration rather than abandonment.

column5: lame remnant made a strong nation
column6: The lame are made a remnant and the outcast a strong nation; this gives the commentary's movement from weakness to solidity a collective prophetic form.

column5: save the lame and gather the outcast
column6: God promises to save the lame and gather the outcast; it gives direct prophetic content to aid for those whose movement and social standing are impaired.

column5: spirit sets the hearer on his feet
column6: The spirit enters Ezekiel and sets him on his feet while God speaks; it is a direct scene in which enabling presence produces upright posture.

column5: touch that strengthens a weakened body
column6: A humanlike figure touches the overwhelmed Daniel and strengthens him; this supplies a bodily counterpart to the source's aid turning weakness into steadiness.

column5: peace and strength received after speech
column6: The messenger says peace and be strong, and Daniel reports being strengthened; it adds spoken reassurance to the commentary's supported, non-panicked recovery.

column5: feet made like a deer's; secure heights
column6: God gives the speaker agile feet and sets him securely on heights; it reframes restored walking as divinely given bodily surety.

column5: right hand supports the speaker
column6: God's right hand supports the speaker; it is a close biblical counterpart to the commentary's claim that aid is a support under a vulnerable person.

column5: broad footing; ankles do not slip
column6: God makes room for the speaker's steps so the ankles do not give way; it specifies secure footing as the result of help.

column5: God gives strength and sure feet
column6: God is the speaker's strength, makes the feet like a deer's, and enables walking on heights; it closely combines strength, gait, and difficult terrain.

column5: level path of the righteous
column6: The path of the righteous is level because God makes it level; it supplies a Hebrew formulation in which moral rightness and an even route converge.

column5: God leads in the way one should go
column6: God teaches what is beneficial and leads the people in the way they should go; it is a direct prophetic response to the plea ihdina.

column5: walk securely; foot does not stumble
column6: The wise person walks securely and does not stumble; it gives the commentary's restored gait a wisdom counterpart.

column5: lead me in the path of commandments
column6: The psalmist asks to be led in the path of God's commandments; this is a direct first-person prayer for guidance alongside ihdina.

column5: establish my steps in your word
column6: The psalmist asks God to establish the steps in the divine word; it joins the source's standing and walking imagery to a petition for firm footing.

column5: Wisdom helps those who seek her
column6: Wisdom instructs her children and gives help to those who seek her; it explicitly joins sought assistance to instruction and guidance.

column5: pray that the Most High direct your way
column6: The sage tells the reader to pray that the Most High direct the way in truth; it is a close Jewish wisdom analogue to asking for the straight path.

column5: Moses' raised hands interpreted as dependence
column6: The talmudic reading of Exodus 17 says Moses' hands did not themselves win the battle; Israel prevailed when they turned their hearts upward, turning bodily support into worshipful dependence.

column5: supports used to undergird a ship
column6: In a storm the sailors use supports to undergird their ship; this gives the commentary's avn as what one relies on a literal structural and travel-related enactment.

column5: worship while leaning on a staff
column6: Jacob worships while leaning on the top of his staff; it brings worship, bodily support, and the vulnerable traveler's staff into a single Christian-scriptural image.

column5: taken by hand, raised, then serves
column6: Jesus takes the fevered woman by the hand and raises her, after which she serves; the scene sequences aid, upright recovery, and service like the source's linked worship and help.

column5: Jesus takes a hand, raises, and the boy stands
column6: Jesus takes the boy's hand, raises him, and he stands; it closely parallels the source's hand-supported body becoming upright.

column5: traveler left half dead on the road
column6: The traveler falls among robbers and is left half dead; this supplies the vulnerable roadside condition to which the Samaritan's assistance in the existing scene responds.

column5: lost sheep carried on shoulders
column6: The shepherd places the found sheep on his shoulders; it offers a pastoral image of carrying one unable to return by its own strength.

column5: come over and help us
column6: A Macedonian man asks Paul to cross over and help them; the request makes aid both communal and tied to a journey across a boundary.

column5: servant made to stand by the Lord
column6: The servant stands or falls before the master, yet the Lord is able to make the servant stand; it brings service, dependence, and uprightness into one statement.

column5: do not place a stumbling block before the blind
column6: The law prohibits placing a stumbling block before the blind; it gives the source's guided weak traveler a negative ethical counterpart, removing what causes a fall.

column5: curse on making a blind person stray
column6: The curse falls on one who makes a blind person wander off the road; it casts the source's needed guidance as a communal obligation not to misdirect the vulnerable.

column5: communal petition for protection from testing
column6: The plural prayer asks not to be brought into testing and to be delivered from evil; it forms a Christian liturgical companion to the communal request for guided protection.

column5: do not put obstacle in a brother's way
column6: Believers are told not to put a stumbling block or obstacle in another's way; it turns the source's safe path into a responsibility toward a fellow walker.

column5: weaker members of the body are indispensable
column6: The body's apparently weaker members are indispensable; it deepens the commentary's body-and-support image by making weakness a condition for mutual care.

column5: able to help those being tested
column6: Because Jesus suffered when tested, he is able to help those tested; it offers a Christological account of help arising from shared vulnerability.

column5: restore, strengthen, establish, and found
column6: God restores, strengthens, establishes, and founds believers after suffering; the cluster gives the source's wall, pillar, and uprightness images a Christian form.

column5: lordly service enacted by washing feet
column6: Jesus the Lord washes disciples' feet and commands reciprocal service; it joins the source's worship-and-help pair to a concrete care for the body's walking members.

column5: strength for endurance and patience
column6: Believers are strengthened with power for endurance and patience; it gives the source's aided, unhurried walking an inward ethical correlate.

column5: ask God to give what God commands
column6: Augustine asks God to give what God commands before commanding what God wills; it is a classic Christian interpretation of obedience as requiring the very aid the worshiper petitions for.

column5: an angel strengthens Jesus in prayer
column6: The angel strengthens Jesus during prayer, closely joining supplication and enabling aid; the verses are absent from some early witnesses, so this candidate requires textual verification.
